minutes.headline: Planning Board took no vote on Tri Town Landing's senior building and continued the hearing to June 11 after height and parking objections.
minutes.summary: The board found a deck expansion at 7 Trillium Court to be a non-material change. It then heard Great Bridge Properties' proposal to combine two remaining Tri Town Landing buildings into one four-story senior building with many waivers. Members and abutters raised height, parking, fire access and privacy concerns, and the hearing was continued. The board also backed a stormwater grant letter, approved minutes, and discussed the marijuana bylaw timeline and the failed special permit time-limit article.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board took no vote on the Tri Town Landing senior building and continued the hearing to June 11 after height, parking and fire access concerns.
The board gave informal guidance on the project: supportive of an age restriction and a density decrease, concerned about the four-story height; no vote on waivers.
The board found the deck expansion at 7 Trillium Court to be a non-material change by voice vote.
Abutters said a fourth floor would look into backyards, and raised unnotified abutters, visitor parking, tree removal and lighting.
A motion on a stormwater 319 grant support letter was made, but the vote was not audible; the town's half of the match comes from road improvement money earmarked for stormwater.

why_it_matters: A four-story, waiver-heavy senior building at Tri Town Landing would change height, parking and fire access for neighbors and the housing mix, and the board has not yet decided on any of it.
The stormwater grant match would use road improvement money earmarked for stormwater, so it draws on the town budget, mostly taxes, rather than a new appropriation.
watch_next: June 11: the Tri Town Landing hearing resumes, with a staff technical review the week before.
A marijuana bylaw listening session, planned for June with town counsel invited.
